title: Russian search engine Yandex struggles after Ukrainian strikes on data centres
key_facts: Yandex, which runs Russia's most popular search engine plus a food-ordering and taxi app, said two of its five data centres were struck by Ukrainian drones in the past two days.

The Sasovo data centre (Ryazan region) was 'seriously damaged' overnight into Thursday and its operations 'completely suspended'; the Kaluga data centre was hit on Friday morning and part of its infrastructure taken out of service.
Yandex said it is 'very difficult to predict' when the sites will be back online; some AI chatbot functions were temporarily unavailable and smart home devices may have problems, it told Tass.
Sasovo houses two of the three supercomputers used to develop Yandex's AI model; it is unclear whether they survived. Kaluga is one of Russia's largest data centres.
Ukraine's defence ministry confirmed the attacks; President Zelensky said Kyiv was responding 'in a mirror-like fashion' to Russian strikes on Ukrainian data centres.
Last month a Russian drone hit a Kyiv business centre, killing four people and damaging a data centre; about 100,000 households lost internet.
No Yandex employees were injured; the Kaluga governor said nine people were injured in a drone attack on the city's infrastructure.
quote_evidence: Yandex said that its data centre in Sasovo, in the Ryazan region, had been "seriously damaged as a result of a drone attack" overnight into Thursday, with its operations "completely suspended".
Zelensky said Kyiv was responding to similar Russian attacks on Ukrainian data centres in a "mirror-like fashion".
why_it_matters_hint: Data centres are now targets on both sides, and Yandex's AI development and services are disrupted.
event_date: Overnight into Thu 8 Oct 2026 (Sasovo) and Fri 9 Oct 2026 morning (Kaluga)
notes: Follow-up of our 8 Oct edition item 34 (Reuters, first strike, attacker not named). New today: second site hit, Ukraine's defence ministry and Zelensky confirm.
